title: Unary index walk
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $w$ and $u$ be Boolean words, let $s$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $w$, let $a,c\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $n\in\mathbb N$, and let $j\in\mathbb Z$. Suppose $w$ is the concatenation of a prefix, the doubled word obtained by repeating $n$ true bits, and a suffix. Starting from the canonical evaluation configuration with prefix length as the input-head position, semantic phase $2$, truth bits $a,c$, skip flag cleared, and certificate-head position $j$, the evaluator reaches after $2n$ steps the canonical configuration with input-head position increased by $2n$, certificate-head position $j+n$, and the same phase, truth bits, and cleared skip flag.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
$s$ is a saved configuration of $M$ on input $w$
The input $w$ is a prefix followed by the doubled word of $n$ true bits followed by a suffix
replaced:
Suppose the evaluator's input contains, at the current position, the doubling of a
unary run $1^n$. In the index phase, exactly $2n$ steps consume the doubled run,
advancing the input position by $2n$ and the certificate head by $n$, leaving the
phase and both accumulator bits unchanged. (The first one of a literal is consumed
by the clause phase, so this scan counts the variable index itself.)
